overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: withholding of 2016–2017 litigation-related executive session minutes and the periodic review practice were lawful. Two other allegations were declined as untimely or as broad audit requests.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission improperly withheld 2016 and 2017 executive session minutes in response to her records request.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that it was appropriate to continue to withhold those executive sessions minutes from public disclosure until the matters had concluded.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to conduct periodic reviews of its executive session minutes at reasonable intervals.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Administrator, as the Commission's designee, conducts a monthly review of the Commission's executive session minutes, we find that the Commission complies with this requirement under the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged, from 2016 to early 2018 minutes, that the Commission did not follow procedural requirements for convening in executive session under Purpose 6.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we decline to review these allegations.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged from 2015 to present that open and executive session minutes lacked a list of documents and exhibits used at meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to review this allegation.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
